renderings.value: Describes something that is decided, arranged, or expected.

The ～ことになっている grammar point is used to express that something has been decided or arranged, or is expected as a rule or custom. It can be translated as 'it is decided that...', 'it is arranged that...', or 'it is expected to...' in English. The formation is used with verbs in their dictionary form.
Verb-dictionary form + ことになっている
ことになっている: a rule or arrangement set by others (～ことになっている).
In this company, it is decided that work will end at 8 pm.
In Japan, it is decided that people 18 years old and above will vote in elections.
At school, it is decided that students will wear uniforms.
It is decided that Tanaka will be the project leader this time.
